name: RelayNook
subtitle: Coding agent alerts & hooks
description:
RelayNook receives events from coding agents and alerts you when a session needs input or finishes. Agents send events through a local URL scheme with an installation token, and you can use the same route for error and informational events as well as updates about sessions that finish or need your input.

You can see how many sessions are waiting for input and choose which events trigger notifications. Sound is optional. The last 200 events stay in local history until you clear them or newer events replace them.

Copy a setup snippet for Claude Code hooks, Codex CLI completion notifications or a generic shell function, then paste it into your configuration. Codex notifications support turn completion only. Waiting alerts need an agent that sends waiting events, so support for those alerts depends on the hook you configure. RelayNook doesn't inspect processes or read transcripts.

Incoming events are rate limited, and repeated notifications are combined for a short interval. Notification delivery also follows your macOS Focus and sound settings.

Use Sample mode to explore fictional events. The test event action checks local processing and notification settings, while a no-install Terminal command checks system URL delivery. Test each configured agent separately to check its hook.

Event data stays on your device, with no account, analytics or remote service needed, and Launch at Login stays off until you enable it.

review_notes:
# Review RelayNook

Requires macOS 14. Launch RelayNook.app. No account or external coding agent is required to test it. Open the menu bar and toggle Sample mode to explore fictional history without credentials. Turn Sample mode off to restore live history and test notifications. Select Send test event. An info event appears in history. In Settings select Enable notifications to request permission; enable individual kinds and optional sound. System Settings and Focus control delivery.

Select Copy Terminal test command. Run that complete command in Terminal. A waiting event appears and the badge increases. Replace kind=waiting with kind=done and run again. The badge decreases. Remove the token parameter. Rejected increases without storing the URL text. Regenerate token invalidates old commands. Clear deletes local history and waiting session identifiers; delivered notifications are managed in Notification Center.

Setup offers optional Claude Code, Codex CLI and generic shell snippets. Users copy and install these themselves. Optional snippets use system Perl with modules for JSON parsing and text encoding for data parsing; they do not use Apple events. The app does not run shell commands, modify external configurations, inspect processes or read transcripts. Codex completion notifications do not report waiting. Hooks report response completion, not project completion. Agent compatibility depends on the agent's hook interface.

The only entitlement is com.apple.security.app-sandbox. Public APIs provide notifications and optional launch at login; no network, Apple events, file access exceptions or usage-description permissions. UserDefaults CA92.1 stores a random installation token. Container JSON stores preferences, 200 recent events and waiting session identities. Serial asynchronous persistence flushes on Quit.

Settings and About expose Privacy Policy and Support links to the final HTTPS pages configured in Info.plist.

Store screenshots use isolated Sample data. the actual popover and Settings tabs with fictional events. No screenshot displays saved history or displays a real token. --smoke writes fresh sandbox verification evidence. --screenshots renders the three images.
